sq.ANSWER:
• Syntax refers to the structure or form of code—how symbols, keywords, and characters are arranged according to language rules.

    • Example: In C++, int x = 5; is syntactically correct, but int = x 5; is not.

  • Semantics refers to the meaning of the syntactically correct statements—what the code does.

    • Example: x = y + z; is syntactically correct, but if y and z are not defined, it has a semantic error.

Key Difference:

  • Syntax errors are caught at compile time, while semantic errors may be detected at runtime or result in incorrect behavior.

import java.sql.*;

public class TopStudents {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String url = "jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/college";
        String user = "root";
        String password = "admin";

        Connection con = null;
        Statement stmt = null;
        ResultSet rs = null;

        try {
            // Load driver
            Class.forName("com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver");

            // Create connection
            con = DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, password);

            // Create statement
            stmt = con.createStatement();

            // Execute query
            rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT name, department, marks FROM students WHERE marks > 80");

            // Process result
            while (rs.next()) {
                String name = rs.getString("name");
                String dept = rs.getString("department");
                int marks = rs.getInt("marks");
                System.out.println(name + " | " + dept + " | " + marks);
            }
        } catch (Exception e) {
            e.printStackTrace();
        } finally {
            try { if (rs != null) rs.close(); } catch (Exception e) {}
            try { if (stmt != null) stmt.close(); } catch (Exception e) {}
            try { if (con != null) con.close(); } catch (Exception e) {}
        }
    }
}
